runs.t: This page lists every cookie RepCheck sets, everything it stores in your browser, and why. It covers the RepCheck app and the iOS app, which is the same site in a native shell.
Do we ask for cookie consent?
No, and here is the reasoning, so you can check it. Under Thailand's PDPA and the EU/UK ePrivacy rules, consent is required for storage that is
necessary to deliver the service you asked for — chiefly advertising and cross-site tracking. RepCheck sets none of that:
anywhere in the app, and no advertising or marketing cookies.
— no Google Analytics, no Meta pixel, no Segment, Mixpanel, Amplitude, Hotjar or similar. Nothing on any page reports your behaviour to another company.
your data, and nothing here is used for profiling or automated decisions about you.

What is left is the strictly necessary cookies listed below, and some local storage that holds your own training data on your own device. Those are exempt from consent — but you are still entitled to know about them, which is what the rest of this page is for.
Both first-party, both strictly necessary, and neither one tracks you across other websites.

Most of what you log lives in your browser's local storage as well as on our servers, so the app still works when your connection drops. This is not a tracking mechanism — it is your training data, on your device, readable only by RepCheck. It includes your workout log, nutrition log, weight log, saved analyses, coaching profile and HYROX history, plus small preferences like your theme, language and units, and how far you got in the app tour.
Clearing your browser's site data for RepCheck, or deleting the iOS app, removes all of it from that device. Doing so does not delete your account — see

The typefaces the app uses (Inter and Noto Sans Thai) are served from our own servers, not from Google's font CDN. That matters more than it sounds: loading them the usual way would make your browser contact Google on every page — including the sign-up page, before you had agreed to anything — and hand over your IP address to do it. They are local instead, so that request never happens.

How to refuse or remove them
Every browser lets you block or delete cookies and site data in its settings. Because the

cookie is what holds your login, blocking cookies for RepCheck means you will not be able to stay signed in — the app cannot work without it. If you would rather not have an account at all, the honest answer is not to create one.
If we add or remove a cookie, this page changes with it and the date at the top moves.

Where it goes, and where it is stored
Your data is stored on our servers, hosted with Render. The providers above are largely based in the

Those transfers rely on your consent and on the contractual terms and standard data protection clauses those providers offer. If you are not comfortable with that, the AI features are the ones to avoid — the rest of the app does not depend on them.

You can delete your account at any time from

After the 30 days, your account and everything attached to it — training logs, nutrition logs, progress photos, saved analyses, custom foods and exercises, friends, challenges and race times — are permanently erased and cannot be recovered.
You can view and correct your account details in Settings, and you can delete individual logs, photos and saved analyses at any time without deleting your whole account.
Beyond what the app lets you do directly, you have the right to ask us to: give you
of it in a portable form;
to how we use it; and
where we relied on it. These are your rights under Thailand's PDPA, and we extend the equivalent GDPR and UK GDPR rights to users in the EU and the UK.
. Asking costs nothing, and we will not treat you differently for asking.

If you think we have handled your data badly, please tell us first — it is the fastest way to get it fixed. You also have the right to complain to a regulator without going through us: in Thailand, the
Office of the Personal Data Protection Committee (PDPC)
; in the EU or UK, your national data protection authority, which in the UK is the

Passwords are stored hashed, never in plain text. The site is served over HTTPS, the session cookie cannot be read by page scripts, and the login and AI endpoints are rate-limited. No system is perfect: if we discover a breach affecting your personal data, we will notify you and the regulator as the PDPA and GDPR require.

RepCheck is not intended for children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect data from them. Because RepCheck handles health data, a young person old enough to use it but still a minor where they live — under 20 in Thailand, or under the age of digital consent in their EU or UK country — needs a parent or guardian's consent first. If you believe a child has given us data, email us and we will delete it.
If this policy changes materially, the updated date at the top of this page changes with it.

There is nothing to buy in RepCheck today. There are no subscriptions, no in-app purchases, no one-off unlocks and no paid tiers. We do not ask for a card, and the app contains no payment system of any kind.
So there is nothing to refund, and this page has no charges to describe. If you are ever asked to pay for RepCheck by anything claiming to be us, it is not us — please
What the free app costs you

Some features cost us money to run, so they have daily limits per account rather than a price: form analysis, food photo analysis and coach chat each have a fixed number of uses per day. Hitting a limit is not a prompt to pay — there is no way to pay. It resets.
If we introduce a paid plan
We intend to add an optional paid plan after RepCheck is released on the App Store. The free features you use today are not being taken away to make room for it. When that happens, and
This page will be replaced with full refund and cancellation terms, and the date at the top will change.
The price, the billing period and what renewal costs will be shown to you on the purchase screen, before you confirm — never after.
Purchases made through the iOS app would be handled by
, not by us. That means Apple takes the payment and Apple issues the refunds, through
. We are not able to refund an Apple purchase directly, and we will say so plainly rather than leaving you to find out.
You would be able to cancel at any time, keep access until the end of the period you already paid for, and not be charged again.

Any statutory right you have to cancel or be refunded — under Thailand's consumer protection law, or the EU/UK right of withdrawal for consumers — applies on top of all of the above. Nothing we publish here can take those away, and nothing on this page is intended to.

RepCheck's AI coach, the workout chat and the Analyze chat answer questions about training, recovery, mobility and nutrition. They are instructed to base their answers on established exercise science, and
every answer lists the sources it draws on, with links, directly under the reply
This page collects every source those answers can cite, so you can read the evidence for yourself.

RepCheck gives general fitness information, not medical advice, a diagnosis or treatment. AI answers can be wrong. Talk to a doctor or other qualified health professional before starting a new training or diet programme, especially if you have a medical condition, are pregnant, or are recovering from an injury. Stop exercising and get medical help if you feel chest pain, dizziness, shortness of breath beyond normal effort, or sharp or lasting pain.

Your nutrition targets are calculated with a fixed formula, not by the AI: resting energy use from the Katch-McArdle equation (based on your weight and estimated body fat), multiplied by a standard activity factor, with protein set per kilogram of lean body mass in the ranges recommended by the
WHO guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour

RepCheck is provided as-is for personal training use. You need an account to use it, you are responsible for keeping your login details safe, and you are responsible for what you upload. You must be at least 13 to have an account, and if you are under the age of majority where you live you need a parent or guardian's permission — see the
RepCheck is free. There is nothing to buy in the app and no payment system in it. Some AI features have daily per-account limits instead of a price. See the
for what happens if we ever add a paid plan.

RepCheck's form analysis, coaching, calorie estimates and training plans are generated automatically, including by AI, and are estimates rather than professional advice. They are not medical advice, not a diagnosis, and not a substitute for a doctor, physiotherapist or qualified coach. Training carries risk of injury. Use your own judgement, and talk to a doctor before starting a new training or nutrition programme — especially if you have an existing condition or injury.
Calorie and macro estimates from photos, rep counts and form scores are approximations and will sometimes be wrong. Do not rely on them for medical or clinical decisions.

The videos, photos and logs you upload stay yours. You give us permission to process them in order to run the features you asked for — analysing a lift, estimating a meal, generating a plan. That permission is limited to running those features and ends when you delete the content or your account; we do not take a licence to publish, sell or advertise with your content. See the

Do not upload content that is illegal, that you do not have the right to upload, or that contains other people who have not agreed to it. Do not use a display name intended to harass or impersonate. Do not try to break, overload or work around the app's limits and security. Accounts that break these rules can be suspended.
You can report or block an account from a leaderboard or your friends list. Reports are reviewed within 24 hours. See
if something is not covered by the in-app report.
You can delete your account at any time from Settings. See the
for exactly what is erased and when. We may suspend or end an account that breaks these terms, and we will tell you why where we are able to.
Changes to the app and to these terms

RepCheck is actively being built, so features change and some may be withdrawn. If we change these terms materially, the date at the top of this page changes with it. If you keep using RepCheck after that, you are accepting the new version; if you would rather not, you can delete your account.

To the extent the law allows, RepCheck is not liable for injury, loss or damage arising from using the app, including from relying on its estimates or generated plans. Nothing in these terms limits liability that cannot be limited by law — including for death or personal injury caused by negligence, for fraud, or any of your rights as a consumer that a term cannot remove.
